title: Choose the visual world for Storage
question: The roll assigned the All-Weather Field Book. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: All-Weather Field Book
options.lineage: waterproof surveyor's field books: yellow covers, numbered pages, gridded level-book columns, an index up front
options.thesis: Your storage, logged like a survey: every box a numbered page, every item a ruled line, built to be used in a dusty garage.
options.viewport: Phone: a yellow cover band with the current box number huge, the box's page below as a gridded list of item lines with photos, and a yellow thumb bar holding Scan and Add.
options.risk: Committed yellow is loud; if the grid and type are timid it reads as a theme rather than a tool.

raised.raise: A persistent bottom bar keeps Scan and Add in thumb reach, and red is reserved strictly for what can be pressed.
A low-light attic mode: dark page, amber pencil, the scanned record ringed so it reads under a headlamp.
States are pencil marks, not badges: checked out is struck through with initials and date, a moved item carries a ruled arrow.
Hierarchy by scale contrast alone: record numbers set enormous, everything else small and quiet.
Every item cell is a photo with a name plate and a one-line note ruled beneath it.
Labels and numbers are set at fixed sizes, never shrunk to fit; long names wrap instead.

options.label: Label Stock
options.lineage: die-cut thermal labels, ZPL printer fonts, Code 128 and QR grammar
options.thesis: The app is made of the same thing it prints: every screen is a label on a liner.
options.viewport: Phone: records stacked as die-cut labels on a pale liner strip; the selected one peels up; Scan sits like the printer's feed button.
options.risk: The literal reading of the product; monochrome can feel like a printout rather than an app.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.thesis: Soft cards, friendly labels, one bright color only where you can press.
options.viewport: A single column of item cards with a persistent bottom bar.
options.case: Holds clarity for a household on phones; loses on identity: it could be any app.

options.label: Midnight Transit Diagram
options.thesis: Locations as lines, boxes as stations.
options.viewport: A line diagram of locations with boxes as stops.
options.case: Storage has no routes; the metaphor costs clarity and nobody here thinks in lines.
options.kept: Fixed-size labels that never shrink to fit.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.lineage: celestial charts read by red flashlight
options.thesis: Items plotted as stars by importance.
options.viewport: A dark chart of the catalog.
options.case: Beautiful, but finding a drill is not stargazing.
options.kept: A low-light mode for dark attics.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference Page
options.thesis: Records set as an annotated edition.
options.viewport: Twin columns around a rail of record keys.
options.case: Desktop reading world; wrong for one-handed phones in a garage.
options.kept: States as printed marks instead of badges.

options.label: Variable Type Specimen
options.case: No connection to storage beyond its discipline.
options.kept: Enormous record numbers, everything else small.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.thesis: Items as a cast of characters.
options.viewport: A pastel grid of item portraits.
options.case: Too cute for a garage tool, but its grid of portraits with captions fits item photos.
options.kept: Photo cells with a name plate and a one-line note.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean home-inventory app like Sortly or Homebox, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Tab bar, search on top, recent items as photo cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other inventory app by design.
